scope: Public cases explicitly reporting use of morluto/rea; source review only, no independent reproduction.

cases.title: DX-Ball: reconstructing stereo sound panning
cases.author: REA showcase team; original project authors credited in sources
cases.target: DX-Ball 1.07 Windows i386 executable
cases.question: How does an on-screen position become a sound-pan value?
cases.rea_role: REA and Ghidra inspect the target function, callers, instructions and constants. The maintainer’s reconstruction explains an x87 expression omitted by the decompiled pseudocode.
cases.reported_result: The source records 3,205 differential cases against the original x86 function and a complete 63-byte match after recompilation with the historical compiler.
cases.limitations: Validation covers one function and a specific checkpoint. The updated showcase reuses earlier execution and compilation records; it does not establish a complete game reconstruction.
cases.takeaway: When pseudocode is incomplete, follow callers, assembly and constants. Record semantic tests separately from byte matching.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Recorded analysis: REA 4.1.0, Ghidra 12.1.4, Linux x64 host.

cases.title: Notion: tracing the Electron rich-text clipboard bridge
cases.author: REA showcase team; original project authors credited in sources
cases.target: Notion Desktop 7.6.1 app.asar and a web-editor module cached at a different time
cases.question: How does a web editor write rich text through the desktop clipboard?
cases.rea_role: REA statically analyzes the tab preload to locate the context bridge and IPC invocation. Direct reading of bundled code fills in the clipboard API, channels and main-process receiver.
cases.reported_result: The showcase explains renderer → preload → IPC → main at source level and demonstrates rich-text markers and Markdown tables in an independent module probe.
cases.limitations: The REA graph did not automatically resolve the full clipboard-channel chain. The web editor and desktop package are not matching runtime samples; real copy/paste was not captured on the same version.
cases.takeaway: Separate structures returned by REA, conclusions from manual code reading and results from independent probes.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: The published npm REA 4.1.0 package inspected the saved tab preload on 7 October 2026

cases.title: TH04: recovering PC-98 bullet-ring angles
cases.author: REA showcase team; original project authors credited in sources
cases.target: Touhou TH04 PC-98 DOS MZ, 16-bit real-mode program
cases.question: How are bullets evenly distributed around a ring and aimed toward the player?
cases.rea_role: REA and Ghidra check the loading layout, analyze helper functions and read instructions and raw bytes. The existing reconstruction project supplies context for fixed-point angles, integer division and wrapping.
cases.reported_result: The showcase presents new REA checks alongside historical Turbo C++ verification: a 2,139-byte region containing the helper matches.
cases.limitations: The historical source reconstruction and compilation checks belong to the TH04 project. The new REA investigation is only part of the evidence, not proof of full-game equivalence or sole REA authorship.
cases.takeaway: Confirm the loading model and address mapping on old platforms, then connect algorithm explanations to compiler checks.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: The page adds a fresh inspection of the supplied original target through REA on 7 October 2026.

cases.title: Aegis: finding the Android TOTP algorithm
cases.author: REA showcase team; original project authors credited in sources
cases.target: Aegis Authenticator 3.4.3 Android APK
cases.question: How is a six-digit login code calculated every 30 seconds?
cases.rea_role: REA Android analysis locates generation, display and copy methods. The author reads the HOTP/TOTP calculation and builds a browser demo with an adjustable clock.
cases.reported_result: The official page reports 133 cases comparing the extracted method with an independent implementation, plus the six SHA-1 reference vectors from RFC 6238.
cases.limitations: The scope is code generation, not a reconstruction of the vault, encrypted storage or the whole app. This catalog did not rerun the cases.
cases.takeaway: Choose a small feature that can be verified independently and constrain its implementation with public standard test vectors.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Inspected with REA 6.1.0 on 9 October 2026.

cases.title: DownUnderCTF: recovering flag-checking equations
cases.author: REA showcase team; original project authors credited in sources
cases.target: DownUnderCTF 2023 masked squares flag checker, stripped Linux ELF
cases.question: How can input validation be recovered without symbols or source code?
cases.rea_role: REA finds prompt strings and cross-references, analyzes the checker and reads masks and target tables. Z3 solves 26 constraints; process capture checks the original challenge binary.
cases.reported_result: The official record shows Correct! / exit 0 for the correct candidate and Incorrect! / exit 255 for an incorrect candidate. The solution is then checked against the organizers’ source and metadata.
cases.limitations: The solver assumes a common flag format and character set. A second-model search timed out, so uniqueness was not proved.
cases.takeaway: After static reasoning produces a candidate, run both correct and incorrect inputs through the original program.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Fresh inspection and process captures on 8 October 2026, using the published REA 4.1.0 package

cases.title: Desktop Games: porting a desktop toy to macOS and the browser
cases.author: ucodia
cases.target: Gemtree’s 2000 Desktop Games / Stress Reducers Windows program
cases.question: How can the Peter interpreter, program tree, interactions and assets be understood and ported?
cases.rea_role: The author uses Claude Code, REA and Ghidra. REA investigates image compression, resource layout, timing, sprite movement, sound and coordinates in the interpreter; Python tools process the program tree and assets.
cases.reported_result: The public repository includes a Swift macOS version, browser version, decompiled program tree and asset-processing scripts.
cases.limitations: The author uses true color instead of the original palette and changes shadow rendering. Inclusion does not verify complete compatibility or redistribution rights for third-party assets.
cases.takeaway: For software with an embedded interpreter, distinguish the interpreter, program tree and assets.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: The interpreter was decompiled with REA

cases.title: Ski or Die: rebuilding Snowball War in Rust
cases.author: tuunanet
cases.target: Snowball War minigame from the DOS edition of Ski or Die
cases.question: How can throwing, collision, spawning and scoring rules be recovered from a DOS game?
cases.rea_role: REA CLI and the Ghidra 16-bit adapter inspect an unpacked MZ load image. Caller-declared code seeds and trace/function/search queries investigate the modules.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes a playable Rust + SDL2 reconstruction, behavior specifications, reverse-engineering notes and asset-extraction tools.
cases.limitations: Only Snowball War is reconstructed. There is no audio playback or side-by-side comparison with the running DOS original; frame rate and PRNG behavior are approximated. Assets must come from the reader’s own game copy.

cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Every analysis call therefore ran through the REA CLI

cases.title: Sketch (formerly paper-rs): a Paper-inspired Rust infinite canvas
cases.author: michaelshimeles
cases.target: Behavior of the Paper desktop design application
cases.question: How can canvas, layout and editor interactions inform an independent design tool?
cases.rea_role: The author states that REA and Claude Code were used to investigate Paper’s desktop behavior before implementing a separate Rust app with wgpu, winit and egui.
cases.reported_result: The project publishes an infinite canvas, pages, layouts, vector editing, whiteboarding and MCP interfaces, with tests and feature differences. Reviewed on 2026-10-21: it is now named Sketch, with the sketch-rs executable, first-launch migration of the old project directory and compatibility with old files and environment variables. It remains one case.
cases.limitations: The author explicitly had not launched it on real macOS hardware. Some features are approximated or missing. Inclusion relies on the author’s public attribution, not verified equivalence to Paper.
cases.takeaway: Learn behavior and interaction contracts while stating the boundaries of the independent implementation.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: by studying the behavior of the Paper desktop app with REA and Claude Code

cases.title: rec-rs: an OBS-inspired native macOS recorder

cases.title: terminal-rs: a market terminal informed by TradingView interactions
cases.author: michaelshimeles

Reviewed on 2026-10-21: 151 built-in indicators, parameter and boundary-input tests, and a macOS universal release script were added. cases.title: Wispr Flow: a speech-input teardown and a small local prototype
cases.author: az9713
cases.target: Wispr Flow 1.6.1102 Electron package and native helper
cases.question: How are recording, transcription, context and pasting connected?

cases.reported_result: The author publishes a teardown, supplementary Ghidra investigation, development record and local flowlite.py prototype.

cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Wispr Flow, reverse engineered with REA

cases.title: hexgrab: investigating the PowerToys color picker
cases.author: iammukeshm
cases.target: Color-picker binaries distributed with Microsoft PowerToys
cases.question: How do global hotkeys, pixel sampling and the clipboard work together?

cases.reported_result: Public source and docs/rea-findings.md are provided. The author reports that 8 of 9 findings were fully correct.
cases.limitations: Tested only on one monitor at 125% scaling; mixed-DPI multi-monitor behavior was not tested on real hardware. The 8/9 result is the author’s check of this investigation, not a general REA accuracy rate.
cases.takeaway: Practice on software with public source so that tool findings can be checked.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: to study how the Color Picker in Microsoft PowerToys works from its shipped binaries

cases.title: AdamTerm: investigating Ghostty’s shell and building a terminal
cases.author: AdamLinCodes
cases.target: Ghostty 1.3.1 macOS app bundle
cases.question: How are the terminal core, native windows, menus and services divided?

cases.title: Ledger Reborn: a local ledger informed by QuickBooks research
cases.author: lxistired
cases.target: QuickBooks Desktop for Mac

cases.reported_result: The author applies findings to dB commands, parameter names and linear/dB conversion, and provides CMocka tests.
cases.limitations: REA’s role is limited to specific vendor-library findings and subsequent improvements, not the whole driver. The mute wire code was not recovered.

cases.title: Virtual Desktop Streamer: a Linux port through a replacement platform layer
cases.author: cudanexus
cases.target: Official Virtual Desktop macOS and Windows installation packages
cases.question: How can capture, encoding, audio and input move to Linux while retaining the protocol library?

cases.reported_result: The public Linux port includes source, build instructions and simulated-headset tests using PipeWire/X11, GStreamer and uinput.

cases.title: OpenBSD netcat: static analysis of a shipped ELF
cases.author: NullLabTests

cases.reported_result: The author publishes function, string and call-path investigations, results.txt and raw JSON output under files/.
cases.limitations: This is static analysis of a specific build. Imports and pseudocode alone do not establish every runtime behavior or constitute a security certification.
cases.takeaway: Keep raw REA output alongside independent tool checks so conclusions can be reviewed.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: We ran two providers against the same image and cross-checked with readelf, objdump, nm, and strings.

cases.title: REA on REA: investigating the tool and testing predictions
cases.author: az9713
cases.target: Installed rea-agents 6.3.0 package
cases.question: How does REA choose a native-analysis provider and detect an unavailable provider?
cases.rea_role: REA statically analyzes five of its own directories. The agent writes falsifiable predictions, runs doctor, then reads the source answers and assesses its predictions.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes the process and test receipts: all four answers were only partly correct, and three of eight predicted Ghidra-check outcomes were wrong.
cases.limitations: A single self-assessment; doctor tests are not open_binary tests. The installed package and source checkpoint also differ.
cases.takeaway: Turn plausible explanations into testable predictions and publish failures.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: REA analyzed 5 folders of the installed rea-agents 6.3.0 package with analyze_javascript_application.

cases.title: rea-groundtruth: checking analysis blind spots against known source
cases.author: UnknownHacker1
cases.target: MongoDB Compass 1.43.4 and handwritten Electron fixtures
cases.question: Does a report of zero IPC calls or windows reflect the app or an analysis gap?
cases.rea_role: REA 6.4.0 analyzes an app with known source. Minimal examples with different webpack wrappers provide controls.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes a one-command reproduction of Electron APIs missed in a particular webpack form and records how a post-signing ASAR integrity mismatch was handled.
cases.limitations: The report concerns specific builds on Windows 11 and REA 6.4.0. Later versions may fix the issue; this catalog does not claim the historical bug persists in the latest version.
cases.takeaway: Zero findings do not establish absence. Fixtures with known source can test analyzer coverage.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Tested with rea-agents 6.4.0 on Windows 11 x64, Node 22.22.

cases.title: rea-lab: measuring REA’s contribution to Windows reverse engineering
cases.author: pablodiazjorge
cases.target: Small Windows challenges, larger binaries with decoys and real open-source programs
cases.question: How does adding REA affect an agent’s success rate, time and cost?
cases.rea_role: The author sets up Windows and Ghidra, runs preregistered controlled studies, verifies cited Evidence and publishes writeups, environments and upstream fixes.
cases.reported_result: Five preregistered studies are public. Study 1: 28/30 in both groups. Study 2: 11/24 without REA versus 4/24 with REA. Study 3: 71/72 versus 68/72. Study 4 uses DeepSeek: 20/20 versus 19/20, with no significant difference detected. In Study 5, the revised skill costs 14% more than the official skill (p=0.012), without a significant accuracy change. The 2026-10-21 Evidence-retention note distinguishes 482 study runs, 336 that called REA and 3 restart-interrupted reruns: none of these 339 REA-calling runs proactively retained Evidence; the grader reconstructed it from client records.
cases.limitations: All studies pin REA 6.4.0, Claude Code 2.1.296 and their respective models, tasks and permissions; results cannot be generalized to current versions or all reverse engineering. Study 2 and 3 success-rate differences were not statistically significant under the author’s tests. Study 3 Evidence certification was corrected from 142/144 to 144/144 after a grader fix; solve counts were unchanged. Study 4 has only 20 pairs. Study 5 compares skill text injected into prompts, not automatic client loading. This catalog did not rerun the studies. The 339 count is REA-calling runs, not the total study sample, and does not imply missing Evidence content or failed certification.
cases.takeaway: Evaluate controls, task distribution, cost and evidence quality together.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Study 1, preregistered: on ten small Windows crackmes, rea did not change how many Claude Code solved

cases.title: rea-playbook: turning Electron Evidence into a report and reconstruction
cases.author: jinshi666888
cases.target: An eight-file minimal Electron example included in the repository
cases.question: How can large Evidence JSON become readable facts and a checked reconstruction?
cases.rea_role: The project pins REA 6.3.0 and supplies an analyze → extract → verify pipeline, MCP handshake and real tool-call probes.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes a sanitized Evidence fixture, file:line report, reconstruction and assertions, reporting 10/10 reconstruction checks passing.
cases.limitations: The offline demo reads an existing fixture; it is not a fresh REA run. A small self-built target does not represent a complex commercial app.
cases.takeaway: Start with a controlled small sample and connect evidence, readable specifications and regression checks.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: npm run analyze will fetch rea-agents@6.3.0 on first use via npx fallback.

cases.title: DiskLens: checking disk-scanning and treemap algorithms in a released binary
cases.author: KarlssonChristoffer
cases.target: WinDirStat 2.5.0 Windows executable and public source
cases.question: How can disk scanning, treemaps and duplicate detection be checked before building a new interface?
cases.rea_role: Claude Code uses REA and Ghidra on the installed WinDirStat.exe to confirm directory enumeration, the NTFS MFT reader, treemap defaults and SHA-512 deduplication. The author states that algorithm details mostly came from reading source; REA checked the released binary and guided the investigation.
cases.reported_result: The project publishes a Rust engine, Tauri/Svelte interface and REA Evidence IDs. The author reports 24 engine tests and a scan/treemap check of roughly 1.3 million files on one machine.
cases.limitations: The author explicitly did not review the generated code. Several file operations and system integrations lack real-UI checks. Fast MFT scanning is absent and hard links are double-counted. Some algorithms directly port GPL source, so this is not a clean-room reconstruction of closed-source software. Single-machine timing is not a controlled performance comparison.
cases.takeaway: Attribute binary observations and source reading separately, and state which file operations were actually tested.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Claude used REA on the WinDirStat 2.5.0 installed on my PC

cases.title: Hyper3D: from captured web bundles to an independent 3D prototype
cases.author: payswapdotorg
cases.target: Captured Hyper3D Rodin JavaScript bundles and workspace behavior
cases.question: How can interface and API observations inform a prototype that exports 3D models?
cases.rea_role: The author uses rea-agents 6.5.0 to statically analyze 21 captured JavaScript files for initial visual-prototype clues. Later functionality is designed separately from authenticated-workspace network observations and an API blueprint. REA did not recover the original 3D-model weights or generation backend.
cases.reported_result: The project publishes a Next.js 16 prototype, API blueprint and differences. The author reports 67 tests covering image/text-to-scene specifications, three.js geometry and GLB, GLTF, OBJ, STL and USDZ export.
cases.limitations: The default generator uses an independent scene-planning and deterministic-geometry pipeline, not equivalent Rodin model quality or backend behavior. External generation services require separate credentials. 3D Editing and WorldGen are not implemented. REA’s contribution is limited to initial web analysis; tests are author-reported.
cases.takeaway: Distinguish frontend observations, API contracts and independent functionality. Export-format tests do not establish generation-quality equivalence.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: rea-agents@6.5.0 analyze-javascript-application

cases.title: Pixel Watch: an eSIM handoff helper informed by companion-APK analysis
cases.author: AllMySlop
cases.target: Google Pixel Watch companion Android APK 5.0.0.958206140
cases.question: How can a separate helper find and open the companion app’s existing watch-eSIM download flow?

cases.title: PicoPrint: connecting a mobile thermal printer to Windows printing
cases.author: bigtower17
cases.target: LX-D02 Bluetooth thermal printer and Funny Print React Native Android app
cases.question: When a driver connects but does not print, how can handshake differences be found?
cases.rea_role: In REA discussion #4152, the author says REA 6.5.0 provided doctor, ADB device checks and the Android investigation entry point. Actual Hermes bytecode decompilation used hermes-dec; protocol inference and traffic comparison were not REA-only work.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes a thermoprint-based Go printing service and protocol notes, reporting Ctrl+P printing of text, images and documents on Windows 11 with a real LX-D02, and an upstream handshake fix.

cases.title: bzip2: checking stripped-binary findings against a symbolized build
cases.author: CassieFox23
cases.target: bzip2 1.0.8 compiled with gcc -O2 and stripped, Linux x86-64
cases.question: How can a function be found from an output string and its call relationships checked?
cases.rea_role: REA 6.4.0 and Ghidra locate a function from a string, list callers and callees, and return Evidence labeled observed/derived. The author separately checks an unstripped build from the same source with source code, nm and objdump.
cases.reported_result: The author reports finding uncompress with 1 caller and 24 callees matching the reference build. Build steps, trimmed MCP records and two classes of error responses are public.

The complete client script is not public; the archive has a recorded hash but no signature verification. This catalog did not rerun it.

cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: REA's function, one caller and 24 callees all matched an unstripped build and the source.

cases.title: A local 27B model: a smaller MCP tool list enables function analysis
cases.author: CassieFox23
cases.target: Self-built C token checker; Qwen3.8-27B, llama.cpp, OpenCode and REA MCP
cases.question: How can REA tool descriptions and analysis fit into a local model’s 32K context?
cases.rea_role: The author uses PR #3026 commit d993ffeb1 and Ghidra 12.1.4. Tool families and an OpenCode allowlist expose only 10 REA tools; the model opens the target, locates and decompiles the function, then closes the session.
cases.reported_result: The author reports that all 206 tool descriptions exceeded context. A 62-tool setup hit a GPU reset after reading the prompt. The 10-tool prompt used 4,407 tokens; three runs found the target string and explained the checker, each taking about 80 seconds.
cases.limitations: The three runs repeat one tiny program and prompt, not three independent tasks. No other model or client was compared. Results use a historical PR commit; tool counts, switches and timings are not guarantees for the current release.
cases.takeaway: Measure schema context cost before testing a minimal tool set. Repetition on one task does not establish general capability.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: With the full tool list, nothing fits.

cases.title: Open-source REA Lab: pinning an npm artifact and analyzing its entry slice
cases.author: martinlofranodeoliveira
cases.target: Official npm rea-agents 6.4.0 package.json and scripts/rea.mjs
cases.question: How can a release artifact be identified before answering a bounded entry-file question?
cases.rea_role: An independent Python auditor checks archive structure and hashes first. REA statically analyzes two unchanged files extracted from the verified package. Entry-branch semantics also use manual syntax checks; the auditor and manual conclusions are not REA output.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes pinned digests, audit JSON, sanitized Evidence summaries and reproduction scripts. The slice reports 1 parsed JavaScript file, 469 AST nodes, 14 findings and zero parse failures, while noting that full-package analysis was interrupted during semantic expansion.
cases.limitations: The 14 findings are not a vulnerability count. The slice retains 110 semantic unknowns and lacks dist implementations, so it cannot establish full-package security or runtime correctness. A sanitized summary is not replayable canonical Evidence; full-package coverage is partial. This catalog did not rerun it.
cases.takeaway: Bound the question and input while retaining interruptions and unknowns. Structural checks, byte identity and runtime safety are different conclusions.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Can REA statically parse the actual shipped dispatcher?

cases.title: ReaFuse: combining two libraries after investigating their behavior
cases.author: sickpyramid
cases.target: Two pairs of open-source JavaScript libraries: ms + pretty-bytes, and dequal + klona
cases.question: How can two projects become behavior specifications and then a new combined tool?
cases.rea_role: REA 6.4.0 JavaScript static analysis reads the two inputs. README files and tests help produce behavior specifications; the model separately proposes combinations, writes acceptance contracts and new code, then runs the author’s tests and similarity scans.
cases.reported_result: The author publishes ratewise (transfer rate and ETA) and objdelta (structural diff/patch), reports and Evidence. Reported contract results are 18/18 and 17/17, plus 7/7 and 6/6 tests for the new tools. Both examples count as one project case.
cases.limitations: Only two public JavaScript examples were reviewed; the project is v0.1 alpha. The same workflow produces specifications and implementations. The author’s clean-room label is not an independent legal conclusion. Similarity scans and passing tests do not establish general originality or complete equivalence. This catalog did not rerun them.
cases.takeaway: Connect analysis to implementation through behavior specifications, mapping tests to either input behavior or the new combination.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Every donor goes through REA's static JavaScript analysis

cases.title: OpenBattlefield2: function-level Evidence for a Battlefield 2 client
cases.author: Moxnatiy
cases.target: Battlefield 2 1.5 Refractor 2 client, rendering DLLs and original game data
cases.question: How can crosshair, HUD and binary-behavior research inform a traceable engine implementation?
cases.rea_role: REA 4.1.0 and Ghidra 12.1.4 read 32-bit PE files and collect full function Evidence dossiers. Direct Ghidra queries, game data and server symbols supplement this. Crosshair notes include GuiIndex, position and offset-accumulation addresses and REA Evidence IDs; REA handles only the analysis stage.
cases.reported_result: The project publishes a C++20 engine, function notes, tests and screenshots. The author reports loading an owned BF2 1.5 installation, connecting to an original dedicated server and displaying soldiers and HUD. In connected mode the crosshair renders, expands during movement and contracts when stopped, with checks such as test_weapon_hud.
cases.limitations: The research project still lacks firing, vehicle driving and sound. Crosshair weapon-switch, zoom and firing updates remain unfinished; hosted mode has no crosshair. The main platform is macOS arm64, and the Windows build was not run. Results involve multiple tools and cannot all be attributed to REA. This catalog did not rerun it.
cases.takeaway: Connect addresses, Evidence, implementation and acceptance commands for one observable feature.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Addresses are BF2.exe unless named otherwise; the evidence IDs are REA’s

cases.title: GunZRs: identifying a packing boundary before rebuilding from game data
cases.author: OpenRsG
cases.target: GunZ: The Duel Steam installation, Gunz.exe and .mrs archives
cases.question: How can reconstruction continue when a packed executable prevents static recovery of game logic?
cases.rea_role: REA and Ghidra investigate native files. The author records Themida sections, entry RVA and unpacking stubs in Gunz.exe, with local REA Evidence paths. Game formats are then mainly recovered from data-file structure. Public scripts also cover REA queries, generated ELF/PE fixtures, analysis, caching and failure propagation.
cases.reported_result: The project publishes a Rust + Bevy reconstruction, format notes, query scripts and tests. The author reports Linux playability with an owned installation, maps, actions, bots, a browser build and LAN. Generated ELF/PE function analysis and snapshot-replay checks are recorded separately from game compatibility.
cases.limitations: The packed game code was not statically recovered, and some behavior and timing are inferred. Original Evidence remains local to the author; public material includes descriptions and scripts. Windows/macOS CI builds are reported but were not played by the author. Map counts have different note scopes and do not prove full compatibility. This catalog did not rerun it.
cases.takeaway: An analysis failure can still establish a useful boundary: label binary facts, data-file observations and inferences separately.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: stub (REA evidence under .local/re/a076a5d8…/). Game code is not statically readable

cases.title: V5VPN: protocol research for a scoped portal and tunnel client
cases.author: hygkui
cases.target: LeadSec V5VPN 5.3.3.x client and v2.0 gateway protocol
cases.question: How can authentication, resource discovery and connection research inform a scoped independent client?
cases.rea_role: The author explicitly cites morluto/rea as a reverse-engineering reference and documents symbols, disassembly and memory mappings in SecUI.exe, SecController.dll, SecLogin.dll, SecSSL.dll and VpnServ.exe. The README connects authentication, password-expiry branches, resource discovery and HTTP CONNECT to an independent Go/MyGo implementation; full REA call logs are not public.
cases.reported_result: Public Go/MyGo desktop and CLI source, protocol notes and tests are provided. The author reports end-to-end connectivity on a Windows development machine and two production gateways, covering the SSL VPN portal, authorized resources and HTTP CONNECT tunnels.
cases.limitations: Reported scope is 5.3.3.x and protocol v2.0. Linux/macOS were compiled but not tested. No kernel virtual adapter, IPsec or whole-network routing; USB Key, anonymous login and Chinese cryptographic suites are unsupported. This catalog did not connect to gateways or verify security and does not treat “fully cracked” wording as an established conclusion.
cases.takeaway: Separate protocol scope from platform tests. Client usability requires validation against specific gateways and scenarios.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: 基于 REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) 逆向分析技术与 MyGo 跨平台桌面技术架构，重新实现的现代化 V5VPN 客户端。

cases.title: Co-op Anything: investigating campaign multiplayer entry points
cases.author: cranebeaker and community contributors
cases.target: Steam C&C3 Tiberium Wars / Kane’s Wrath builds and World in Conflict client/dedicated server
cases.question: How can a campaign retain its scripts and sides while letting a second player join?
cases.rea_role: C&C3 notes explicitly record REA/Ghidra 12.1.4 observations of the TW 1.10 executable, locating the function that removes campaign sides during multiplayer/skirmish preparation. World in Conflict notes document dedicated-server role-selection analysis through REA/Ghidra, separating single-player restrictions, server state and unverified inferences. Other scripts, debuggers and runtime tests handle later work.
cases.reported_result: The project publishes MCP/skills, synchronization-test tools and game-specific research. C&C3 notes include addresses, formats and experiments. For World in Conflict, the author reports a LAN campaign host running missions while a second client joins and sees live synchronized units, but cannot control its own units. Each game retains its own QA level.
cases.limitations: REA attribution is limited to the reviewed C&C3 and World in Conflict investigations, not every mod in the directory. Player-two control, deployment zones, visibility and internet play remain unfinished in World in Conflict; the report verifies LAN only. C&C3 also has unresolved campaign failures and context issues. Stars do not prove a completable campaign. This catalog did not run the games or tests.
cases.takeaway: Validate client connection, synchronized visibility and genuinely playable co-op as separate outcomes.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: Engine seams (observed in the TW 1.10 exe with REA/Ghidra 12.1.4)

cases.title: sparkDash: integrating REA analysis into a multi-device dashboard
cases.author: MiaAI-Lab
cases.target: REA CLI, input files and analysis/Evidence views on remote Linux devices
cases.question: How can a web interface submit long-running remote REA jobs and load large results on demand?
cases.rea_role: The project actually calls upstream REA through its CLI, pinning rea-agents 6.4.0 and its lockfile. server/rea implements detached jobs, uploads, status, paged results and exports. Commands drive inspect-analysis-view and compare; the dashboard does not implement a decompiler.
cases.reported_result: The public Tools → REA page and server implementation support detached remote execution, logs, summaries, limitations/unknowns, on-demand views, JSON exports and Evidence comparison. Version pinning, job-management and upload tests are public. Inclusion concerns implemented integration, not installation instructions alone.
cases.limitations: This is an integration case, not a REA reconstruction of sparkDash or proof that every upstream analysis path passed hardware acceptance. Devices must run Linux, the feature is off by default and target formats need additional providers. Reviewed manager tests use fake REA and a local shell, which do not replace real Ghidra or remote-device tests. This catalog did not install or run it.
cases.takeaway: Attribute upstream capabilities separately from scheduling and UI work, preserving evidence, limitations and failures in the displayed results.
cases.rea_evidence_excerpt: sparkDash uses the CLI only

cases.title: Open Claude UI: documenting desktop interactions and publishing reusable UI components
cases.target: Claude Desktop macOS package; author-reported @ant/desktop 2.37337.1 baseline and bundled web UI
cases.question: How can input composition, scrolling and desktop interaction rules inform reusable interface components?
cases.rea_role: The author attributes ASAR, JavaScript AST and CSS investigation to REA 6.5.0. The interaction chapter links bundled-code excerpts to input guards and scrolling rules; separate TypeScript examples implement those behaviors.
cases.reported_result: The repository publishes versioned design notes, a component storybook, CSS tokens and implementation examples, including composition-state checks and a post-composition Enter guard in RichComposerWithMentions.tsx.
cases.limitations: This is a UI library and author-reported teardown, not a complete Claude client or model service. Raw REA session records and independent behavioral or visual equivalence tests were not found in the reviewed files. Version and fidelity claims remain the author’s.
cases.takeaway: Connect one interaction rule to its cited bundle location and implementation; distinguish design documentation from measured equivalence.

cases.title: Open Scrantic: rebuilding the Johnny Castaway screensaver engine in Rust
cases.target: Screen Antics: Johnny Castaway (1992), Windows 3.1 SCRANTIC.SCR and matching resource files
cases.question: How can a 16-bit screensaver’s script interpreter, story schedule and random behavior run on modern systems?
cases.rea_role: The developer explicitly credits Claude Code with REA for disassembling and decompiling SCRANTIC.SCR, recovering resource formats and script semantics, and producing the Rust implementation and documentation.
cases.reported_result: The public Rust engine implements resource loading, TTM/ADS script execution, story progression, timing and the original random-number generator. ENGINE.md records recovered rules and deliberate differences; the author supplies Windows, macOS and Linux release paths.
cases.limitations: The engine requires the user’s own matching original files and rejects other executable builds. Full-frame redraw, optional image/audio processing and settings differ from the original. Cross-platform behavior and equivalence were not independently tested here; raw REA sessions were not found in the reviewed files.
cases.takeaway: Keep original asset ownership separate from engine code, preserve arithmetic and scheduling rules, and document deliberate compatibility differences.

cases.title: REA Safe Agent: brokering static analysis between two contained processes
cases.target: REA 6.7.0 integration with Ghidra 12.1.4 and JADX; benign ELF fixtures and an F-Droid APK
cases.question: How can an agent query REA while access to inputs, host tools and model requests remains bounded?
cases.rea_role: The implementation runs REA and its receiving agent in separate Docker containers and relays allowlisted MCP calls through a host controller. Frozen input snapshots, tool/path checks and bounded results constrain what crosses the boundary; REA supplies the actual static analysis.
cases.reported_result: Dated macOS ARM64 receipts report 11 successful REA calls with Claude and 9 with Codex on the same benign ELF, checking its hash, FNV-1a constants and decoded string against known source. The validation record separately reports 39 successful REA calls for a live F-Droid 2.0.2 analysis.
cases.limitations: These are author-published receipts, not an independent security certification. Static analysis does not execute the target. Containment depends on Docker and the host controller; analyzed text reaches the model service, and Windows Docker integration is experimental. Whole-image vulnerability findings remain despite the separate clean npm audit.
cases.takeaway: Separate mock-policy tests, real tool calls and live model runs; attach each claim to a dated target, host and receipt.

cases.title: REA in Spanish: reconstructing an author-owned key validator
cases.target: Author-owned educational licencia-cli.stripped binary and its symbolized reference build
cases.question: How can a small stripped program’s acceptance rule be reconstructed and checked against the original?
cases.rea_role: The author reports using REA and Ghidra pseudocode plus bytes read at 0x102040 to recover character conversion, weighted accumulation, rotation and acceptance checks, then writing a separate Python verifier.
cases.reported_result: The free Spanish sample includes lab setup and a worked case, stripped and symbolized practice binaries, reference C source and a reconstructed Python verifier. The verifier lists 4 expected examples; the author reports checking the reconstruction against the real binary.
cases.limitations: The exercise is the author’s own small unprotected program, not a commercial licensing bypass or a general result for protected software. The 4 examples are limited checks, not exhaustive equivalence. This catalog did not execute the binaries or rerun the comparison; the proposed full course is not yet delivered.
cases.takeaway: Use an owned fixture with a hidden reference source, recover one bounded rule, and test accepted and rejected inputs before comparing with the source.
